explanation: Retrospective, context-free detector for the GPT-NeoX letter/symbol pieces: at layer 0 the pole is a pure function of the current token id (a token reads the same in every context, whatever surrounds it) and it peaks on the bare lowercase letter 'r' (2.832, its scan max), then grades with how character-like the piece is: other bare lowercase consonants at 0.54-0.93 of max (j, l, b, k, c, d, m, h, n, p, t, f, v, g, q, z, x, w in that order), bare vowels and weak letters at 0.14-0.48 (i, u, y, s, e, o, a), space-prefixed single letters at 0.00-0.81 (' r', ' b', ' m', ' c', ' l', ' d', ' j', ' t' and ' n' above 0.70; ' h' 0.69, ' s' 0.51, ' i' 0.28, ' e' 0.07, ' a' 0.00), single capitals at 0.20-0.66 (R, L, B, C, N, J, T, M, D, K, H, V highest; Q, Z, S lowest), Greek letters as symbols or as bare names at 0.22-0.66 (delta, rho, gamma, chi, lambda, beta, theta, tau, kappa, sigma, nu, mu as symbols; bare tau/gamma/kappa/rho/beta 0.53-0.59, delta 0.43, sigma 0.38) and 2-4 character abbreviation/identifier pieces at 0.15-0.47 (mt, kB, ch, tr, tbl, chr, idx, corr, txt, obj, cfg, src). Everything word-like is silent: ordinary words and word-pieces never exceed 0.35 (the, error, word, struct, source, my, try, yes are below 0.05), 87% of the 50,277-piece vocabulary stays at or below 0.05, digits at most 0.05 and CJK characters at most 0.43, so a piece fires only when it is itself a character or a letter cluster and never merely because it contains the letter 'r'.
